title: Matsushima — 松島
goal: Connect sea scenery with tree/mountain shapes, sky and white.

blocks.text: Matsushima Bay is known for its pine-covered islands. We will look at a fictional photograph rather than give navigation advice. A location chapter may cover a town, district or sightseeing area; it need not be a separate legally designated city.
**松島で海を見ます。** まつしまで うみを みます。 — I look at the sea in Matsushima.
海 was one of the very first Hokkaido characters. Today it supports new nature words. The photograph can contain an island, a mountain, sky and a white cloud, giving each new word a clear reference.

items: **Character:** 松 · **Useful meaning/reading:** pine; まつ, ショウ · **Radical and visible components:** 木, きへん, plus 公, a historical sound component · **Role:** Encounter; tree family link.

**Character:** 島 · **Useful meaning/reading:** island; しま, トウ · **Radical and visible components:** 山, やま; upper shape related to an abbreviated 鳥 · **Role:** Encounter; dictionaries discuss sound and bird/land imagery.

blocks.text: Learn **松島 / まつしま**. 木 inside 松 connects back to 林/森. 山 inside 島 will be studied next. The upper shape is not the complete modern 鳥 character, and it does not guarantee that the island has birds. We are analysing spelling, not proving the place name's origin.

**山 / やま — mountain; 山の上 / やまのうえ — on top of a mountain.** 山 is its own radical, やま. The complete form is mountain-derived; recognise the central peak and the surrounding structure without requiring a literal three-peak landscape.
**あの山は大きいです。** あの やまは おおきいです。 — That mountain over there is big.

山 was an encounter in earlier place-name/登る discussions and in 岩/岡. Now recognise it independently. **小さい山 / ちいさいやま**, a small mountain, reuses the adjective directly before a noun. Actual mountains' sizes are not being compared in this practice picture.

cards.title: From 木 to 松; from 山 to 島

blocks.text: A photograph label says **島 / しま**, island. Another says **松 / まつ**, pine. These are useful assisted words, while today's formal kanji goals remain 山・空・白.
**島に木があります。** しまに きが あります。 — There are trees on the island.
**この木は松です。** この きは まつです。 — This tree is a pine.

A broad tree character becomes part of a more specific tree word; a mountain component can occur in another landscape character. Components connect knowledge across the Journey. They do not make 林, 森 and 松 interchangeable: grove, forest and pine name different things.

**空 / そら — sky; 青い空 / あおいそら — blue sky.** 空 has radical **穴**, あな/あなかんむり, and **工** below it. 穴 can be visually recognised as 宀 above 八-like lower strokes; 工 participates in the historical sound structure.
**空は青いです。** そらは あおいです。 — The sky is blue.
**空を見ます。** そらを みます。 — I look at the sky.

空 has other readings and senses such as empty, but today's word is そら. Do not read the sky word as あな or こう simply because those components are visible. 穴 is a component encounter, not another new vocabulary requirement.

cards.title: 白: A Colour Word and a Shape

blocks.text: **白い / しろい — white; 白 / しろ — white, colour noun.** 白 is its own radical, しろ. Its short upper stroke distinguishes it from 日. Similar outlines do not make the two characters the same.
**白い雲 / しろいくも — a white cloud.** 雲 / くも is assisted vocabulary; its character is not formal study here.
**あの雲は白いです。** あの くもは しろいです。 — That cloud over there is white.
In 白い the final い is an adjective ending. The kana reading しろい belongs to the whole word. We will meet 白 again in Shiroishi's name, where the spelling is combined with 石.

cards.title: Before a Noun or at Sentence End

items: **Phrase/sentence:** 白い雲 · **Reading:** しろいくも · **Meaning:** a white cloud
**Phrase/sentence:** 雲は白いです · **Reading:** くもはしろいです · **Meaning:** the cloud is white
**Phrase/sentence:** 小さい島 · **Reading:** ちいさいしま · **Meaning:** a small island
**Phrase/sentence:** 島は小さいです · **Reading:** しまはちいさいです · **Meaning:** the island is small

blocks.text: For these い-adjectives, retain い before the noun. Compare **きれいな海 / きれいなうみ**, a beautiful sea, using the familiar な-adjective pattern. The final い in the spelling きれい does not make it an ordinary い-adjective. Classify the taught word, not just its final kana.
Imagine three photographs: one beside you, one beside your friend, one across the room.
**この写真は山の写真です。** この しゃしんは やまの しゃしんです。 — This photograph is a photograph of a mountain.
**その写真は海の写真です。** その しゃしんは うみの しゃしんです。 — That photograph near you is a photograph of the sea.
**あの写真は島の写真です。** あの しゃしんは しまの しゃしんです。 — That photograph over there is a photograph of an island.
の identifies what each picture depicts. This combines Aomori's noun modifiers with new nature nouns. “Near you” here addresses the listener.
**私は松島で白い雲を見ました。** わたしは まつしまで しろい くもを みました。 — I saw white clouds in Matsushima.
Breakdown: 私は = narrator; 松島で = place of viewing; 白い雲を = the thing seen; 見ました = saw. Japanese need not mark 雲 as plural.
**友だちも海を見ました。** ともだちも うみを みました。 — My friend also looked at the sea.

も adds the friend to the account. The photograph and narrator are fictional; understanding the grammar is separate from learning cultural geography. Do not infer a transport plan or weather forecast from the story.
**この島は小さいです。でも、きれいです。** この しまは ちいさいです。でも、きれいです。 — This island is small. But it is beautiful.
**山を見ました。そして、海を見ました。** やまを みました。そして、うみを みました。 — I looked at a mountain. Then I looked at the sea.

Both connectors are review from Hiraizumi. でも introduces contrast; そして continues. In an ordinary conversation “small but beautiful” is a speaker's comparison, not a logical claim that small places are usually unattractive. Keep the sentences short and let the connector organise the account.

items: What radical links 松 with 林 and 森? **Answer:** 木.
Read 青い空. **Answer:** あおいそら, blue sky.
Which differs from 日 by the extra short upper stroke: 白 or 山? **Answer:** 白.
Choose “a white cloud”: 白い雲 / 白な雲. **Answer:** 白い雲.
Complete “look at the sea”: 海＿見ます。 **Answer:** を.
Explain whether 山 inside 島 guarantees the name's reading. **Answer:** No; it helps recognition, while 松島 is learned as まつしま.

blocks.text: 松島 is まつしま. 松 contains the familiar tree radical; 島 contains 山. 山 is やま; 空 is そら in the sky word; 白い is しろい. 白 and 日 are different characters. An ordinary い-adjective keeps い before a noun; きれい still uses な there.
**Recall task:** Describe the practice cloud and sky. **Models:** 雲は白いです。空は青いです。 Keep 雲 assisted. Continue to Ishinomaki and reuse the words in place descriptions.
